page: Microsoft Azure FX4-2mds_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the FXmdsv2 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It utilizes the x86_64 architecture and is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with a high base clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 1 physical core supporting 2 threads (2 vCPUs), a substantial 260 MB L3 cache, 84.0 GB of system memory, and a 236 GB local NVMe SSD.

Benchmark data reveals a significant divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The server achieves top-tier single-core performance, as demonstrated by a Geekbench single-core score of 2342.0 and strong single-threaded gzip compression throughput of 34.72 GB/sec. Conversely, due to its single physical core design, multi-core and parallel processing metrics are weak, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 2217.08 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2884.0. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with uncached read speeds at 21.11 GB/sec and write speeds at 14.3 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers an exceptionally high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 42 GB per vCPU, making it highly specialized for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. The inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage provides fast local scratch space. It is best suited for single-threaded or low-concurrency applications requiring massive memory footprints, such as specialized database operations, caching layers, or memory-intensive single-core analytical tasks.
